subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95, concurrency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya@finly.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95, concurrency)

Hi Sam / Maya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed or misstated.

Summary of pain points & goals
- UX: Streaming feels laggy for your support agents — they expect near-immediate partial responses during typing.
- Current observed p95: ~850ms for short responses (under 256 tokens), with occasional spikes >1.5s under load.
- Concurrency: Targeting ~500 concurrent streaming sessions during peak (US business hours).
- Error/timeout tolerance: <5% client-facing failures and graceful fallback for long-tail requests.

Current stack & constraints
- Self-hosted transformer endpoints on k8s (NVIDIA A100s), custom batching layer, nginx ingress.
- Using open model variants without quantization; KV cache not centralized (per-pod), which limits cache hit rates.
- Streaming implemented via HTTP chunked responses; client expects token-level flush every ~150ms for typing UX.

Success criteria (what success looks like for Finly)
- p95 latency (per-message short responses, <=250ms) for typical support prompts (<256 tokens).
- Sustained concurrency of 500 streams with p95 SLOs met and <5% errors.
- Streaming UX: consistent chunked delivery, first token latency <80ms where possible, incremental tokens delivered smoothly.
- Observability: per-route p95, token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs for compliance.

Short-term proposal / next steps
1) Technical deep dive / load test: schedule a 60–90 min session with Aditya to walk your infra and confirm payload shapes and concurrency patterns.
   - Goal: agree on PoC load test plan and pass/fail criteria.
2) PoC: Redwood runs a controlled load test (Finly provides sample payloads and representative concurrency profile).
   - Deliverable: p95 report (latency + errors), token-cost estimate, configuration recommendation (batching, caching, quantization).
3) Commercial discussion: if PoC meets success criteria, propose Dedicated capacity + rollout plan.

Attachments: MOM and sample payload template attached (20270228-finly-discovery-mom.pdf, finly_sample_payloads.json).

Proposed times for the technical deep dive: Wed Mar 2 or Thu Mar 3 (US morning). Let me know which works and I’ll loop in Aditya for the deep dive.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya@finly.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95, concurrency)

Thanks Marissa — solid writeup, appreciate the clarity. A couple quick clarifying questions before we schedule the deep dive: 

1) Streaming behavior: our client expects token-level flushes roughly every 100–200ms. Can Redwood guarantee incremental flushes (not just line-buffered responses) and do you support server-side chunk sizing / early flush?

2) Concurrency model: the 500 sessions target is per-region (US). Is your PoC testable against region-specific capacity? We need to ensure cross-region routing won’t hurt p95 in production.

3) Long-tail requests: some of our agent prompts hit 1k+ tokens occasionally. How do you recommend we handle those while keeping short-response p95 SLOs?

If you can confirm those, I’ll get sample payloads ready for the load test. Wed Mar 2 morning PT would work for us.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform, Finly
sam.patel@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finly.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya@finly.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95, concurrency)

Hi Sam — quick answers inline, and next steps below.

1) Streaming / incremental flush: yes — Redwood supports token-level streaming with configurable chunk sizes and early flush heuristics. For your UX target (100–200ms flush), we typically recommend a combination of small initial chunking (first token within ~80ms) and adaptive flush windows thereafter. We can enable aggressive flushes for short-response routes and more relaxed bundling for long-form generation.

2) Concurrency & region testing: we can run PoC in the US region only. Our routing policies will pin PoC traffic to a dedicated pool so you get a realistic region-isolated test.

3) Long-tail requests: recommended approach is route-based SLOs — short-response routes keep aggressive batching/caching profiles; long-form routes use separate compute pools or fallback models (quantized) to avoid impacting short-response p95. We’ll include a configuration recommendation in the PoC report.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- Wed Mar 2, 09:00–10:15 PT: Technical deep dive with Aditya (we’ll cover payloads, TLS/SAML needs, and test harness).
- PoC load test (Redwood-run): we’ll need sample payloads, representative concurrency timeline, and any SSO/KMS constraints. Expected turnaround: 5 business days after receipt of payloads.

Aditya — can you scope a quick initial capacity/config estimate for 500 concurrent streaming sessions (typical payloads ~150 tokens, occasional 1k+ token spikes)? I’ll confirm the deep dive invite once Sam confirms Wed 9am PT.

Sam — attaching the MOM and payload template; feel free to drop sample payloads directly into the Drive link or reply with a ZIP.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95, concurrency)

Marissa — looping in my quick thoughts (internal).

- Initial estimate: to support 500 concurrent streaming sessions with p95 <=250ms for short responses (~150 tokens) we should provision a dedicated pool equivalent to ~6 A100-80GB GPUs with optimized batching and prefix KV cache shared across pods. If Finly is willing to accept modest quantization on long-tail routes, we can reduce to 4 GPUs for the same cost envelope.
- Need sample payload distribution (80% short <256 tokens, 20% long-form) and exact concurrency ramp to size correctly.
- I’ll prepare a scoped cost/sku recommendation and baseline config by EOD Tue.

I’ll join the deep dive and can run through the PoC test harness and metrics we’ll collect.

—Aditya
